BiblicalUsage: Achan is the man whose sin cost Israel a battle. Joshua 7:1 names him — Achan, the son of Carmi, of the tribe of Judah — and says he took of the accursed thing, and the anger of the LORD was kindled against the children of Israel. The chapter tells the rest: Israel's defeat at Ai, the lots falling on Achan, his confession that he had taken a Babylonish garment and silver and gold from Jericho and hidden them in his tent, and the judgment in the valley of Achor. One man's hidden sin, and the whole camp paid for it.
TheologicalSignificance: A name that carries a warning, not a teaching to invent. Achan shows what one hidden sin does: it does not stay hidden, and it does not stay private. I hold that his story is in the Bible so I remember — the devoted thing in my tent is never only my business.
